note: What each benchmark board measures, for the benchmark page (ticket 25) and model inspection (ticket 12). `measures`, `tasks` and `score` are quoted from the page named in `url`, fetched on `fetched`; a quote may be cut at a sentence boundary but is never reworded. `scale` says what the number on the plot is, read from the row's own field. `cost` is the basis in sources.json. `category` is the source's own grouping where it gives one (Artificial Analysis: Knowledge Work, Coding, Science, General), else the nearest of those. `direction` is curated and is never inferred for a board with no entry. `speaks_to` is curated relevance of the quoted description to coding work, knowledge work and API-workflow evidence; it is not the source's claim, and it does not name a routing Domain or a Class that does not exist. A board with no entry is shown with no description and says so.

Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.measures: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index combines a comprehensive suite of evaluation datasets to assess language model capabilities across knowledge work, coding, science, and general knowledge.
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.tasks: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 incorporates 9 evaluations: AA-Briefcase v1.1, AutomationBench-AA, GDP.pdf, FrontierCode 2.0, Terminal-Bench 4.0, AA-Omniscience v1.1, HLE-Diamond, CritPt v2 (Hard Subset), and Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1.0.
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.score: The Intelligence Index is calculated as a weighted average across four categories: Knowledge Work (25%), Coding (25%), Science (25%), and General (25%).
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.cost: per task: the cost of running the Intelligence Index
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.speaks_to: composite across knowledge work, coding, science and general knowledge; shown and never counted by the carry rule. Each of its nine evaluations is its own board here

AA-Briefcase.measures: AA-Briefcase is a new benchmark for testing models on realistic knowledge work tasks in complex projects built by industry experts.
AA-Briefcase.score: Combined Elo from pairwise comparisons on rubric-graded task success, analytical quality and presentation quality
AA-Briefcase.cost: per task: this board's own cost, from the Index's per-evaluation breakdown
AA-Briefcase.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: multi-week expert projects with thousands of source files, graded on deliverables. Coding work: adjacent to impl only as long agentic file work

AutomationBench.measures: It tests whether models can complete realistic SaaS workflows that span multiple simulated business apps, using REST APIs as the tool interface.
AutomationBench.tasks: We evaluate a private 657-task held-out split from AutomationBench dataset version 1.0.6. The tasks cover six business domains: Finance, HR, Marketing, Operations, Sales, and Support.
AutomationBench.score: For the headline score, a task receives 0 if the model violates any guardrail. If no guardrails are violated, the task receives the percentage of objectives the model completed. Errored tasks also score 0.
AutomationBench.cost: per task: this board's own cost, from the Index's per-evaluation breakdown
AutomationBench.speaks_to: API-workflow relevance: REST-tool SaaS workflows, not GUI computer use. Adjacent to mechanical and impl only as multi-step tool calls against a spec; not a routing Domain or Class

GDP.pdf.measures: a benchmark that tests whether models can reason over long, real-world professional documents and satisfy task-specific criteria.
GDP.pdf.tasks: 100 tasks across ten professional domains, grounded in 4,592 PDF pages and graded against 1,275 criteria.
GDP.pdf.score: All-pass is the headline metric: the share of all 500 attempts where every criterion passes.
GDP.pdf.scale: share of attempts where every criterion passes, 0 to 1
GDP.pdf.cost: per task: this board's own cost, from the Index's per-evaluation breakdown
GDP.pdf.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: long professional PDFs, no tools. Coding work: scout and review at most

Terminal-Bench 4.0.measures: The 4.0 release of Terminal-Bench, developed by Stanford University researchers, the Laude Institute, and the open source community. Covers software engineering, system administration, data processing, model training, and security, with each task graded by its own verification suite.
Terminal-Bench 4.0.tasks: We evaluate the full Terminal-Bench 4.0 dataset (66 tasks) using the mini-swe-agent harness, with pass@1 scoring averaged over 3 repeats per task
Terminal-Bench 4.0.score: a task passes only if every test passes, grading runs in each task's own separate verifier container isolated from the agent's environment, and a verifier that exceeds its timeout counts as a failure
Terminal-Bench 4.0.cost: per task: this board's own cost, from the Index's per-evaluation breakdown
Terminal-Bench 4.0.speaks_to: Coding relevance: the model alone in one neutral harness (mini-swe-agent); the tbench board scores each harness's own agent. Coding work: impl and hard-impl

FrontierCode 2.0.measures: FrontierCode 2.0 is a coding benchmark from Cognition, built with maintainers of open-source repositories. Each task asks an agent to make a change to a real open-source repository, and the benchmark measures whether the change is good enough for a maintainer to merge.
FrontierCode 2.0.tasks: We evaluate all 132 tasks with 3 attempts per task
FrontierCode 2.0.score: An attempt that fails any blocking check, or that the trajectory scanner flags for looking up the solution, scores 0. Other attempts get a weighted score across the rubric's criteria.
FrontierCode 2.0.cost: per task: this board's own cost, from the Index's per-evaluation breakdown
FrontierCode 2.0.speaks_to: Coding relevance: mergeable changes to real repositories, tests plus maintainer rubric. Coding work: impl, hard-impl and review

Terminal-Bench-Science.measures: Its research workflow tasks are drawn from real scientific practice, and experts curate and review each one. Each task has its own set of tests that the agent must pass by working in a terminal.
Terminal-Bench-Science.tasks: We evaluate the full Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1.0 release (70 tasks: 19 life sciences, 17 physical sciences, 17 mathematical sciences, 9 engineering sciences, 8 earth sciences) using the mini-swe-agent harness, with pass@1 scoring averaged over 3 repeats per task
Terminal-Bench-Science.score: A task passes only if every test passes, and grading runs in each task's own separate verifier container isolated from the agent's environment
Terminal-Bench-Science.cost: per task: this board's own cost, from the Index's per-evaluation breakdown
Terminal-Bench-Science.speaks_to: Science relevance: research workflows in a terminal. Coding work: impl in scientific code

CritPt v2 Hard.measures: The hard subset of CritPt v2 is a fixed, private list of 40 of the 70 CritPt problems, selected to remove the 30 problems that seven frontier models solved in all five attempts at the time CritPt v2 was launched.
CritPt v2 Hard.score: then report mean accuracy across repeats (pass@1) on the 40 problems in the hard subset.
CritPt v2 Hard.cost: per task: this board's own cost, from the Index's per-evaluation breakdown
CritPt v2 Hard.speaks_to: Science relevance: research-level physics. Not a coding or knowledge-work axis

Omniscience.measures: AA-Omniscience is a knowledge and hallucination benchmark that measures factual reliability, rewards precise knowledge, and penalizes incorrect guesses or hallucinations.
Omniscience.tasks: The benchmark consists of 3,000 questions covering 42 topics, including Business , Humanities and Social Sciences , Health , Law , Software Engineering , and Science, Engineering and Mathematics .
Omniscience.score: Models are scored using the AA-Omniscience Net Score , which assigns points for correct answers, subtracts points for hallucinated responses, and keeps abstentions neutral, rewarding abstentions over incorrect guesses
Omniscience.scale: AA-Omniscience Net Score, below zero when wrong answers outnumber right ones
Omniscience.cost: per task: this board's own cost, from the Index's per-evaluation breakdown
Omniscience.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: factual reliability and hallucination (42 topics; not a finance, investing or supply-chain split). Coding work: scout and review at most — a wrong fact stated with confidence is the failure it counts

HLE-Diamond.measures: HLE-Diamond is a refined and updated 1,000-question version of Humanity's Last Exam from the Center for AI Safety and Scale AI.
HLE-Diamond.score: We grade each answer with the official HLE judge prompt and response format, using GPT-5.6 Luna (medium) as the judge, with pass@1 scoring.
HLE-Diamond.scale: share of questions answered correctly, 0 to 1
HLE-Diamond.cost: per task: this board's own cost, from the Index's per-evaluation breakdown
HLE-Diamond.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: hard academic reasoning and knowledge with no tools. Coding work: review at most

GDPval.measures: GDPval-AA v2.1 is Artificial Analysis' evaluation framework for OpenAI's GDPval dataset. It assesses language models' capabilities on economically valuable tasks, covering 44 occupations across key sectors contributing to GDP in the United States.
GDPval.score: Pairwise comparison (Elo) by judge panel, anchored to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (max) at 1600, frozen & scaled
GDPval.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost; the page gives this board no cost of its own
GDPval.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: professional deliverables pairwise-graded. Coding work: adjacent to impl as finished files judged against each other, not tests. Standalone since Index v5.0

Harvey LAB.measures: For each task the agent reads the case documents in a sandbox and produces legal deliverables - memos, disclosure schedules, deposition summaries, redlines, and similar work products - in a single run without live interaction.
Harvey LAB.score: Headline is the Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate: the average over tasks of the share of the three-judge panel that passed every rubric criterion, with a task zeroed on any material hallucination, pass@1
Harvey LAB.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost; the page gives this board no cost of its own
Harvey LAB.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: legal deliverables from case documents, hallucination-gated. Not a coding axis

AA-AnalystAgent.measures: AA-AnalystAgent is Artificial Analysis' end-to-end data analysis benchmark.
AA-AnalystAgent.tasks: 80 quantitative questions across 14 business and scientific domains
AA-AnalystAgent.score: LLM judge binary correctness with numeric pre-check override, pass^5
AA-AnalystAgent.scale: share of questions right on all five attempts, 0 to 1
AA-AnalystAgent.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost; the page gives this board no cost of its own
AA-AnalystAgent.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: spreadsheet and document analysis by running Python. Coding work: scout and impl for data scripts

EnterpriseOps-Gym.measures: which evaluates AI agents on stateful, multi-step planning and tool use across realistic enterprise workflows.
EnterpriseOps-Gym.score: Outcome-based SQL state verifiers, strict pass@1 success rate
EnterpriseOps-Gym.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost; the page gives this board no cost of its own
EnterpriseOps-Gym.speaks_to: API-workflow relevance: multi-turn MCP tool use against enterprise systems, graded on final state

APEX-Agents.measures: It evaluates long-horizon, cross-application agent work in professional services environments spanning investment banking, management consulting, and law.
APEX-Agents.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost; the page gives this board no cost of its own
APEX-Agents.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: long-horizon professional-services agent work

ITBench.measures: ITBench-AA is Artificial Analysis' independent implementation of IBM's ITBench benchmark, evaluating AI agents on Site Reliability Engineering (SRE): Kubernetes incident root-cause analysis.
ITBench.score: LLM-normalized entity matching, average precision at full recall
ITBench.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost; the page gives this board no cost of its own
ITBench.speaks_to: Coding relevance: incident diagnosis from logs, traces and topology. Coding work: scout and review

SciCode.measures: Python programming to solve scientific computing tasks.
SciCode.tasks: We test with scientist-annotated background information included in the prompt
SciCode.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost; the page gives this board no cost of its own
SciCode.speaks_to: Coding relevance: single-turn scientific Python with no agent loop. Coding work: mechanical and impl. Legacy since Index v5.0

MLCR.measures: an open benchmark from Wisedocs that measures how well models reason over long, fragmented medical records the way claims professionals do when they review insurance and healthcare cases: reconstructing chronology, causality, treatment patterns, and claim relevance.
MLCR.score: LLM judge panel (3-judge majority: complete, no claim contradicting the record), pass@1
MLCR.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost; the page gives this board no cost of its own
MLCR.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: long medical-record reasoning. Not a coding axis

CritPt.measures: Research-level physics reasoning benchmark with unpublished, frontier physics problems spanning a wide range of subfields.
CritPt.tasks: We implement the 'challenge' level components for all 70 test-set challenges (the example challenge is excluded) in collaboration with the CritPt team
CritPt.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost; the page gives this board no cost of its own
CritPt.speaks_to: Science relevance: research-level physics. Legacy since Index v5.0

Humanity's Last Exam.measures: Recent frontier academic benchmark from the Center for AI Safety (led by Dan Hendrycks).
Humanity's Last Exam.tasks: 2,158 text-only questions across mathematics, humanities, and the natural sciences
Humanity's Last Exam.score: Evaluated with the equality checker LLM prompt from the original HLE implementation, using GPT-5.6 Luna (medium), with pass@1 scoring
Humanity's Last Exam.scale: share of questions answered correctly, 0 to 1
Humanity's Last Exam.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost; the page gives this board no cost of its own
Humanity's Last Exam.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: academic questions with no tools. Legacy since Index v5.0; HLE-Diamond replaces it

tau3-Banking.measures: Fintech customer-support domain of the 𝜏-Knowledge framework developed by Sierra, evaluating agents that must coordinate retrieval from a large unstructured knowledge base with multi-step tool-mediated account changes.
tau3-Banking.tasks: We evaluate the full 𝜏³-Banking task suite (97 tasks) with 5 repeats per task and report pass@1 averaged across the repeats, running the upstream tau2-bench v1.0.1 dataset and grader
tau3-Banking.score: Outcomes are scored against actual backend database state (for example, whether a dispute was opened or a provisional credit issued) rather than conversational quality
tau3-Banking.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost; the page gives this board no cost of its own
tau3-Banking.speaks_to: API-workflow relevance: policy retrieval plus multi-step tool calls, graded on backend state

AA-LCR.measures: Evaluate long context performance through testing reasoning capabilities across multiple long documents (~100k tokens measured using cl100k_base tokenizer)
AA-LCR.tasks: 100 hard text-based questions spanning 7 categories of documents (Company Reports, Industry Reports, Government Consultations, Academia, Legal, Marketing Materials, and Survey Reports)
AA-LCR.score: Model responses are evaluated using GPT-5.6 Luna (medium) as an equality checker with pass@1 scoring
AA-LCR.scale: share of questions answered correctly, 0 to 1
AA-LCR.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost; the page gives this board no cost of its own
AA-LCR.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: long-document reasoning. Coding work: scout and review at most. Legacy: Artificial Analysis no longer runs it on every new model (2026-11-01)

Terminal-Bench 2.1.measures: A verified refresh of Terminal-Bench, developed by Stanford University researchers, the Laude Institute, and the open source community. Keeps the same 89 curated tasks across software engineering, system administration, data processing, model training, and security
Terminal-Bench 2.1.tasks: We evaluate the full Terminal-Bench v2.1 dataset (89 tasks) using the Terminus 2 agent harness in an E2B sandbox environment, with pass@1 scoring averaged over 3 repeats per task
Terminal-Bench 2.1.score: Each task ships with a verification suite that the agent must satisfy by interacting with the terminal — tasks are considered successful only if every test passes
Terminal-Bench 2.1.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost; the page gives this board no cost of its own
Terminal-Bench 2.1.speaks_to: Coding relevance: agentic shell work graded by tests; the task set also spans operations and science, so it is not a pure coding axis. Coding work: impl and hard-impl. Legacy: Artificial Analysis no longer runs it on every new model (2026-11-01)

GPQA Diamond.tasks: 198 questions covering biology, physics and chemistry - we test the GPQA Diamond subset of the full GPQA dataset (448 questions total), which was defined by the original authors as the highest quality subset, where both experts answer correctly and the majority of non-experts answer incorrectly
GPQA Diamond.score: 4 option multiple choice format. Regex-based answer extraction with pass@1 scoring
GPQA Diamond.scale: share of questions answered correctly, 0 to 1
GPQA Diamond.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost; the page gives this board no cost of its own
GPQA Diamond.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: scientific multiple-choice with no tools and no code. Coding work: review at most. Legacy: Artificial Analysis no longer runs it on every new model (2026-11-01)

MMMU-Pro.measures: An enhanced MMMU benchmark that eliminates shortcuts and guessing strategies to more rigorously test multimodal models across 30 academic disciplines
MMMU-Pro.score: Multiple Choice (10 options). Regex extraction, pass@1
MMMU-Pro.scale: share of questions answered correctly, 0 to 1
MMMU-Pro.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost; the page gives this board no cost of its own
MMMU-Pro.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: multimodal understanding of images and text. It does not directly measure coding or API-workflow performance.. Legacy: Artificial Analysis no longer runs it on every new model (2026-11-01)

IFBench.measures: A benchmark that evaluates a model's ability to follow precise instructions in a single turn. It tests a wide range of skills, including counting, formatting, and sentence manipulation.
IFBench.tasks: Uses the single-turn IFBench dataset, which contains 294 questions
IFBench.score: Our score represents the prompt level accuracy (average across all questions and repeats)
IFBench.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost; the page gives this board no cost of its own
IFBench.speaks_to: Coding relevance: following precise instructions in a single turn. Coding work: mechanical — doing exactly what the brief says. Legacy: Artificial Analysis no longer runs it on every new model (2026-11-01)

Terminal-Bench 4.0.measures: Terminal-Bench is a benchmark for measuring agents' abilities to complete tasks using a terminal.
Terminal-Bench 4.0.score: Resolution rate of Terminal-Bench 4.0 tasks. The whiskers span the 95% confidence interval.
Terminal-Bench 4.0.cost: whole run, not per task; the leaderboard does not say so, and sources.json records it
Terminal-Bench 4.0.speaks_to: Coding relevance: an agent and a model scored as a pair ("To test an agent and model, pass --agent and --model"); the task set is not a pure coding axis. Coding work: impl and hard-impl

SWE Refactor Bench.measures: Can a coding agent move a whole repository to a new stack — another language, framework, platform or build system — and change nothing about what it does?
SWE Refactor Bench.score: S(τ) = 1[migration happened] · 1[every check passes] · (0.4 + 0.6 · s/6) ∈ {0} ∪ [0.4, 1]. Behavioural Tests: 130,118 checks recorded from the original. All of them, or the run scores zero.
SWE Refactor Bench.speaks_to: Coding relevance: whole-repository migrations. Coding work: hard-impl — hours-long work on a whole repository
